Update - Donkeys

By: Chwayitisa Futshane | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
... donkeys on the move...

Unique Selling Point:
The rescue of donkeys from the heinous donkey trade fuelled by the Asian market for ejiao.
The mass relocation of 400 animals from Plettenberg Bay to prince Albert Valley

Summary:
The Karoo Donkey Sanctuary operation since 2015 is predominantly dedicated to the rehabilitation of abused donkeys. The donkey trade is a humanitarian issue as it affects poor communities across the African continent, especially women.
Women depend on the donkeys to help them carry firewood, water and other heavy items. In addition, donkeys are used to generate an income.
In some communities, women wake up to find their donkeys have been bludgeoned in the middle of the night.
The slaughter of donkey has also affected the ability of children to get to school on time in rural areas, as they are often forced to assist with the transportation of items donkeys would have carried.
The story is about a love for nature, recognizing the value of each contributor to the ecosystem - including beautiful donkeys.

Further information:
Karoo Sanctuary Facebook Update:
With our monumental relocation now only 4 DAYS AWAY, (my super shattered nerves!!), notwithstanding the financial logistics related to the acquisition of the property in positive progress, I cannot even begin to detail all the precision planning that we have been honing for the past six weeks.
How does one relocate 400 animals, (220 of which are rescued donkeys, horses and cows) disassembled shelters, water troughs, equipment, gates, fencing, feed and no less than 10 loyal management staff and carers and all their personal possessions 260 kilometres over the Swartberg Mountains to our new Promised Land in the sublime Prince Albert Valley in the Great Karoo! You may well ask!
Our two enormous equine floats from Mark's Horse Transport will be leaving Johannesburg for Plettenberg Bay tomorrow, arrival Wednesday afternoon (8 November 2023) for day one of our loading of our first 80 donkeys at sunrise on Thursday morning (9 November 2023). The journey through the mountain passes is estimate to take the best part of 5 hours and grooms will be travelling in the holding area with the donkeys, to ensure all remain calm and stable. We will be running our two equine trucks every day for 5 days until the very last of our rescued beating hearts sets foot on the soil of our new eden.
We will also be positioning an empty 12 meter container at the farm tomorrow morning for the team to begin loading all our inanimate equipment. The container will be transported on a flat-bed trailer across to Prince Albert on Thursday, to arrive before the equine floats to enable us time to set up the necessary water troughs before the arrival
We will also be running three support vehicles back and fourth every day and a huge thanks to Victoria, our volunteer (and equine expert) who has flown in all the way from Romania for two weeks to help us with the relocation and a week on the other side to ensure all the kids are settled in

Case Study:
Jono Sherwin Karoo Donkey Sanctuary

Script:


Donkey Sanctuary Update
VIZ - Location establishers, some donkeys…

VO1: Thousands of donkeys are killed in South Africa each day. (pause)
… It’s a booming international market where the animal’s skins are traded for thousands
of rands

Viz: Donkey Slaughter Episode 4943
Ejiao, 04:48-04:58 Stacked donkey skins; 05:59 - 06:08 donkey carcasses
UPSOUND JONNO SHERWIN
@ 02:52 Donkey Slaughter Episode 4943
We believe they boil the skins then the gelatin rises to the surface, that is then used to make a
tincture

VO2: The trade is fueled by demand in China for what’s known as Ejiao (eh-gee-yow) – an
ingredient in traditional medicine produced from the collagen in the donkey skins.

Viz: undercover cellphone footage of Chinatown in Johannesburg Donkey Slaughter Episode
4943

VO3: Our undercover exposé, in 2017, in Johannesburg’s Chinatown, revealed how
lucrative the market has become..

UPSOUND STORE KEEPER
@ 04:04 - 04:10 Donkey Slaughter Episode 4943
R 10 000 for 1 kilo, R 10 000 for 1 kilo….This one is R 2800

VO4: The donkey skin trade is valued at close to 130 Billion Rand.

UPSOUND GRACE DE LANGE, SPCA Donkey Slaughter Episode 4943
@ 01:34 Grace de Lange, SPCA Donkey Slaughter Episode 4943
It’s very bad we’re starting to receive reports on a weekly basis about animals that are being
slaughtered in the most horrendous manners

VO 5: For the past six years, the Karoo Donkey Sanctuary founded by Jonno Sherwin,
has been taking care of donkeys rescued from the illicit trade at a site in Plettenberg Bay,
in the southern Cape.

@04:26 Jonathan Sherwin, Karoo Donkey Sanctuary
It was certainly never our intention to become the largest donkey or equine sanctuary back then
VO6: The animals they look after have a significant black market value which has made
the sanctuary a target of unwanted – and potentially dangerous – attention.

@12:26 Jonathan Sherwin, Karoo Donkey Sanctuary
…we have had incidents where we've had dodgy visitors come through, wanting to do tours… I
relayed to the team I'm afraid they're not allowed to come in
VIZ:
https://fb.watch/okBlZ7z4kD/ ( Jonno walking with camera as donkeys run up behind him)
VO7:
But, after saving 200 donkeys destined for the slaughterhouse - the team faced another
challenge

00:04:54

…we realized in Plettenberg Bay it was too wet for the donkeys. We lost a lot of donkeys in the
early days due to weather…

VO8: The Plettenberg Bay site wasn’t fit for purpose and had to be sold.

@00:05:22 Jonno Sherwin, Karoo Donkey Sanctuary
We realized we're going to be homeless unless I made a very fast plan.

VO9: Anxious about the animals’ welfare, they searched for an alternative… eventually
finding an ideal farm more than 200 kms away in the Klein Karoo!

UPSOUND JONATHAN SHERWIN INTERVIEW
@09:42 Jonno Sherwin, Karoo Donkey Sanctuary
Planning was I'd say 4 months —-Making sure the animals were fit to travel ...we even
organized a chorus for you guys (donkeys braying in the background) (great interaction

Viz: https://fb.watch/okBA9NO_OR/ (Cellphone footage of Prince Albert Valley)

VO10: At sunrise early last month, the first 80 donkeys were loaded.

@10:06 Jonno Sherwin, Karoo Donkey Sanctuary
One of the greatest challenges is we have a great number of animals in what we call our ICU.
It's always a challenge to travel with them you have to load them tightly in the truck which had
its positives and negatives

VO11: …The journey to their new 580 hectare home required a long and winding road trip
across the Swartberg Mountains.

Viz: Video 6 - the road to Prince Albert valley
Viz: Google Drive: DonkeyVideo 1, Donkey video 2, Donkey Video 4
Jonno voice heard: “Hey Thulas, how’s it going my man - today no scratches no kicks…

VO12: The journey kept the sanctuary’s dedicated team on their toes.
@11:33 Jonno Sherwin, Karoo Donkey Sanctuary
Trucks wise we used probably 11 transporters and two containers of supplies through...four
sprinter vans…
@11:33 Jonno Sherwin, Karoo Donkey Sanctuary
...I was back and forth five or six times

VO14: Relocating the 400 rescued animals, including 220 donkeys, took a toll.

UPSOUND JONATHAN SHERWIN INTERVIEW
@06:23 Jonathan Sherwin, Karoo Donkey Sanctuary
…emotionally you can see I'm a bit haggard it's been really grueling, brutal and certainly
herculean but we just had to focus heads down.

VO13: The relocation took more than six days

Viz: “Truck departing 7” - video of truck leaving as Jonno speaks
@ 0:03 Jonno Sherwin, Karoo Donkey Sanctuary
And there it is folks the end of a chapter, two and half years in Plettenberg Bay …rather
overwhelmed with emotions (Jonno teary) and super excited we are moving onto bigger and
better things

@11:33 Jonno Sherwin, Karoo Donkey Sanctuary
...the cost all in probably about R 300 000 and lots of grey hairs

VO15:
But the sacrifice is worth the result and, with the help of donors, Jono and his team are
determined to continue going.
Viz: https://www.facebook.com/reel/849527996646047 - the donkeys walking through the idyllic
new setting
